description.narrative: Projektstödet till We Effect i Colombia syftar till att underlätta återintegreringsprocessen för kvinnliga och manliga före-detta soldater tillsammans med deras grannkommuner, genom att genomföra hållbara ekonomiska modeller baserade på kooperativa modeller med ett jämställdhetsperspektiv. Stödet är geografiskt inriktat på Montes de Maria-regionen (Sucre, Bolivar och Cordoba), som alla är konfliktdrabbade regioner. Detta stöd är en andra fas av en tidigare insats för återintegreringsprocessen med ID-nummer: 12204.

The project support to We Effect in Colombia has the objective to facilitate the reincorporation process of female and male ex-combatants jointly with their neighbouring communities, through the implementation of sustainable economic models based on cooperative models with gender perspective included. The contribution has its geographical focus in the Montes de Maria region (Sucre, Bolivar, and Cordoba), which are conflict-affected regions. This contribution is a second phase, building on a previous contribution to the reincorporation process with ID-number: 12204

The proposed impact goal is: Sustainable rural development, resilient to climate change, with gender justice and using cooperative models, which reinforce territorial roots and contribute to the reconstruction of the social fabric and a peaceful society in Colombia."
The outcome goal is men and women ex-combatants in a reincorporation process together with their neighbouring communities, implementing sustainable economic models, based on cooperative models and with a gender perspective, guaranteeing access to rights and participation in peace building.
The specific objective is: men and women ex-combatants in a reincorporation process part of social and solidarity economic organizations from municipalities of the Departments of Bolívar, Sucre and Córdoba, their families and communities participate to improve their socioeconomic conditions and help in building peace.
The following three specific outputs are proposed: 1. The women ex-combatants in a reincorporation process from the organizations and communities of the municipalities of Bolívar, Sucre and Córdoba have strengthened their political and economic empowerment and their capacities to recognize and exercise their rights. 2. Women's and mixed organizations, ex-combatants in a reincorporation process, from the social and solidarity economy in municipalities of Bolívar, Sucre and Córdoba, have comprehensively developed and improved sustainable enterprises leveraged by capital, financial inclusion, knowledge management, associativity, alliances and including the gender approach. 3. Organizations, their families and communities in municipalities in Bolívar, Sucre and Córdoba, particularly women and youth, influence public policies to gain access to rights and help strengthen coexistence and local and regional reconciliation.

Over the first seven months of project implementation, We Effect focused on installing the territorial office in Sincelejo. This measure permitted a notable reduction of costs associated to personnel mobilization and, closer coordination with local institutions and organizations who focus their work on peacebuilding, economic development and advocacy initiatives in the region and better communication with FEDECARIBE. Additionally, We Effect has likewise positioned itself as a trustworthy organization that demonstrates significant progress in gender, reincorporation, environmental and economic development domains.
WE presented progress regarding land formalization for Ex-combatants. A ceremony was held on August the 30th with President Petro, the director of National Agency for Land (ANT is it acronym in Spanish), and the Ministry of Agriculture. The Ambassador had planned to accompany this visit. However, at the last minute WE spoke about a problem with the land with communities requesting the property rights over this land. The event was then moved elsewhere and clarification about the property rights and conflict sensitivity is pending.
Between September 15-21, 2023 We Effects board of directors visited Colombia. The Embassy participated in different activities during this visit: 1. Victor Solano traveled to Ovejas on September 16.
2. On September 19, the Ambassador, Victor Solano and Catalina Hoyos participated in a meeting with Swedish companies with a triple objective: on the one hand, for representatives of Swedish companies in Colombia to get to know the delegation and the work of We Effect in Colombia, in particular the support to cooperatives of former FARC combatants in the reincorporation process. On the other hand, for the delegation to hear the perspective of Swedish companies on the investment context in Colombia, with their perspectives on security issues. Finally, to identify possible synergies taking into account the clear aim of the Swedish government to strengthening Sidas work with foreign trade. The meeting was very fruitful, and the three objectives were achieved.
3. The same day, the Ambassador, Victor Solano and Catalina Hoyos participated in a forum about cooperativism where Lotta Folkesson, President of LRF Västerbotten and Anna Carlström, the head of Lantmännen, shared the history of their organizations and some important lessons for cooperatives in Colombia. The main message from Anna was that the objective of their cooperative has been to bring benefits to the members through the profitability of farms. They have adapted their organization to the changing world and have therefore promoted the work in the whole value chain of food, the industrialization to transform the basic agricultural products and then the international trade. The focus on internal democracy has been very relevant to maintain trust among members. Lotta mentioned the Swedish process to ensure land property rights for peasant farmers as the basis for future investments. Former FARC combatants in the reincorporation process highlighted the importance of the cooperative model as an opportunity to create jobs and stable incomes as the basis for the peace building and reincorporation process.
The Embassy's assessment is that this visit was a great opportunity to visibilize in Sweden and to the board, the results and challenges in Colombia that could potentially result in more interest and funds for We Effect in the country. In addition, it was very positive to inspire the cooperatives of former combatants and victims that are part of Fedecaribe and receive support from We Effect. We Effect and the cooperatives are now aware of the importance of the profitability of business models as the corner stone for the sustainability of the cooperative itself. The internal democracy, the incidence, the gender perspective, etc. are very important but if the business model does not work the cooperative will die. The Embassy assessment is that We Effect has had little success in trying to build links with the private sector, market systems and value chains. The second output of this project includes efforts to create sustainable business models with access to capital, financial inclusion, knowledge management, associativity and alliances with local and international organizations, including the Swedish companies. It is expected that the visit by the Board will contribute to that purpose.
